web_blocks.title: Two-Sided Steelman: The Strongest Bull Case vs. The Strongest Bear Case

web_blocks.html: Unbiased underwriting tests both sides at $103.57 [21, 22]. On the Bull side, SK hynix holds 50%–58% HBM share and ~70% initial HBM4 share [15]. LTAs cover >50% of 2027–2028 output, TTM operating margin is 74.52%, and ROIC sits at 54.01% [13, 21]. Yet shares trade at 5.77x trailing P/E and 2.55x forward P/E ahead of Q4 earnings (Jan. 27–28, 2027) and a KRW 100T return plan [21, 28, 31]. On the Bear side, SKHY crashed 13.11% on 39.86M shares to $102.45 inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend [22]. The ADR still embeds a 27.0% premium over $580.01B KRX parity (~$81.58) [21, 22]. Meanwhile, 9M cash conversion fell to 83.7% on KRW 59.12T receivables, capex commitments jumped to KRW 42.71T, and FX swings KRW 7.22T per 10% won move [29].

We assign REJECTED (rejection_reasons: ["TREND", "VALUATION"], conviction_tier: "TIER_0").

web_blocks.title: Held Position Audit (17.764 Schwab Shares): Breached $116.28 Stop Forces EXIT_IMMEDIATELY

web_blocks.html: Our Charles Schwab account holds 17.764 shares of SKHY at a $2,999.99 cost basis ($168.88/share) and zero open options. At the November 20 close of $103.57, that stake is worth $1,839.82 (2.45% of our $75,110.60 net worth). That reflects an unrealized loss of -$1,160.17 (-38.67%). Because $103.57 breached our prior $116.28 stop loss, our upward-only ratchet rule forbids averaging down into Stage 4. We issue EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 17.764 shares (holding_shares_to_sell: 17.764) [22]. Selling today recovers ~$1,839.82 and eliminates exposure to $10.33–$10.34 daily ATR swings (9.98% of close; 8.11% weekly / 6.01% monthly Finviz volatility, beta '-') toward $81.58 KRX parity or $60.06 cycle-compression stress [21, 22, 25].

Proceeds (~$1,839.82) rotate 100.0% into Schwab T-Bill and Money Market cash (~4.76% 2Y Treasury yield) [27]. Shortlist Stage 2 leader McKesson (MCK, $1,069.72, STAGE_2, $1,200.00 base target, 1.69:1 asymmetry) stays at 0.0% today [22]. The S&P 500 sits in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend (38.8% > 50-DMA), and MCK trades slightly above its $985.44–$1,066.70 zone [22]. Outside peer Micron (MU, $594.51, STAGE_4) also stays at 0.0% because it broke below its $912.26 50-day SMA [22].

Decision Trigger: Keep REJECTED (TIER_0, TREND) on new capital and execute EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 17.764 Schwab shares (~$1,839.82 at CMP $103.57) after the $116.28 stop breach. Rotate 100% into CASH (0% MCK, 0% MU). Re-evaluate SKHY only after the US Downtrend ends, Bollinger Band width drops below 18%, and price reclaims $157.01 on >=35.5M shares/day after Jan. 27–28, 2027 earnings [22, 28].

book_paragraphs: Every research cycle eventually reaches the moment where analysis turns into a binding portfolio trade. On November 20, 2026, our rulebook leaves zero ambiguity: SKHY closed at $103.57, breaching the $116.28 structural stop we set on November 13. When a stop breaks, we do not move the goalpost lower to accommodate a falling stock.

Before executing that exit, let us fairly steelman both sides of the debate at $103.57. The strongest Bull Case rests on SK hynix's undeniable AI memory leadership and deeply compressed earnings multiples. SK hynix still commands 50% to 58% of global HBM revenue and roughly 70% of initial HBM4 allocations, with over half of 2027–2028 capacity locked in under long-term agreements. Operating margin sits at 74.52% with 54.01% ROIC, and the ADR now trades at 5.77x trailing earnings and 2.55x forward consensus estimates alongside a KRW 100 trillion FY2026 shareholder return plan.

Yet the Bear Case explains exactly why the tape broke down. SKHY just plunged 13.11% in a single day on 39.86 million shares into a 52-week low of $102.45 inside an S&P 500 Downtrend marked by ten distribution days. Even at $103.57, U.S. ADR buyers still pay a 27.0% premium above TradingView's $580.01 billion Seoul equity valuation (~$81.58 implied parity). Meanwhile, the November 16 Form 6-K revealed that 9M 2026 operating cash conversion fell to 83.7% as trade receivables jumped 225% to KRW 59.12 trillion, unrecognized capex commitments jumped 6.4-fold to KRW 42.71 trillion, and currency sensitivity hit KRW 7.22 trillion per 10% won move.

Let us weigh the 12-month outcomes objectively from $103.57 without propping up fundamental fair value with falling technical averages. Assigning 20% probability to a $157.01 Bull Case (reclaiming the 50-day moving average after January 2027 earnings), 45% to our $73.24 fundamental Base Case (a 50/50 blend of $94.34 cycle-peak $50 billion FCF value and $52.14 normalized $25 billion mid-cycle FCF value), and 35% to a $60.06 Bear Stress Case (closing the 27.0% ADR premium to $81.58 Seoul parity and compressing KRX P/B to the 1.87x 2023 cycle band) yields a primary expected price of $85.38 (-17.6%). Under a Bear-regime stress test—10% Bull at $157.01, 40% mid-cycle FCF at $52.14, and 50% Bear stress at $60.06—expected value falls to $66.59 (-35.7%).

Across all three time horizons—short term, medium term, and long term—our new-capital verdict is REJECTED at TIER_0 due to TREND and VALUATION. Short-term momentum is Stage 4 with zero 4-hour reversal turn; medium-term buyers must wait for basing across the $81.58–$93.48 monitor band (Seoul parity to Pivot S2) and a $157.01 reclaim; and long-term rejection is corroborated by compressed 83.7% cash conversion on KRW 59.12 trillion ending receivables (+KRW 47.44 trillion CFO drag), KRW 42.71 trillion in unrecognized capex commitments, KRW 122.48 trillion of FVTPL assets plus 14.1% Kioxia consolidation volatility, and KRW 10 trillion of buybacks earmarked for employee equity compensation.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Negotiate With a Breached Stop
book_callouts.text: The hardest sell order in investing is exiting a great engineering company after a 38.7% loss. Yet moving a breached $116.28 stop downward at $103.57 is how cyclical drawdowns turn into permanent portfolio scars.

book_subsections.title: Executing EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on Our 17.764 Schwab Shares
paragraphs: In Charles Schwab, we hold exactly 17.764 shares of SKHY at a cost basis of $2,999.99 ($168.88 per share) and zero open options. At the November 20 close of $103.57, that position is worth $1,839.82—a 2.45% portfolio weight and an unrealized loss of $1,160.17 (-38.67%).

Because $103.57 broke below our $116.28 prior stop loss, our upward-only ratchet rule triggers an automatic EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 17.764 shares. Refusing to average down into a high-volatility Stage 4 breakdown (9.98% daily ATR, 8.11% weekly / 6.01% monthly Finviz volatility, beta '-') protects the remaining $1,839.82 from a slide toward Pivot S2 at $93.48, KRX parity at $81.58, or $60.06 cycle-compression stress.

Execution is straightforward: enter a market or tight limit sell order for all 17.764 shares at the next session open, confirm full settlement into the Schwab cash sweep, and clear the position from active risk exposure.

book_subsections.title: 100% Cash Redeployment in an Active S&P 500 Downtrend
paragraphs: Once the $1,839.82 sale settles, 100% of the proceeds move straight into Schwab money-market or T-bill cash earning roughly the 4.76% 2-year Treasury benchmark. Cash is an active, protective allocation when only 38.8% of index stocks trade above their 50-day moving averages and the market carries ten distribution days.

We evaluated Shortlist Stage 2 leader McKesson (MCK at $1,069.72 against a $1,200.00 base target) and outside memory peer Micron (MU at $594.51), holding both at 0% today. McKesson sits slightly above its $985.44–$1,066.70 snapshot support band during a macro Downtrend, while Micron sits in a Stage 4 crash alongside SKHY. Dry powder waits for market breadth to mend.

Keeping 100% in cash also cuts portfolio volatility cleanly across our $75,110.60 net worth. Exiting a Stage 4 memory ADR carrying a $10.33–$10.34 daily ATR (9.98% of close) and 8.11% weekly / 6.01% monthly volatility (Finviz beta '-') lowers equity drawdown sensitivity immediately.

book_subsections.title: Why Cutting a Breached Stop Beats Hoping for Parity Relief
paragraphs: Human nature hates realizing a 38.7% loss, especially when a stock looks optically cheap at 2.55x forward earnings. Yet mathematically, a drop from $103.57 to $81.58 KRX parity would compound the loss from cost basis from -38.7% to -51.7%, and compression to $60.06 (1.87x KRX P/B) would deepen the loss to -64.4%.

Closing the position today frees capital from a broken chart, trims portfolio beta, and lets us re-evaluate SK hynix cleanly after Q4 earnings in late January 2027 if a Stage 1 base forms and the 50-day moving average ($157.01) is reclaimed on heavy volume.

Remember the core lesson of this entire refresh cycle: operational excellence inside Icheon's fabs and risk control inside your Charles Schwab account are two separate jobs. Let the engineers win the HBM4 race while our capital waits safely in Treasury-yield cash until the tape turns back into Stage 2.

book_subsections.title: Exact Execution Checklist and Post-Exit Watchlist Triggers
paragraphs: To leave zero ambiguity when markets open, review our three-step action checklist. First, commit zero fresh equity or options capital to SKHY at $103.57; new capital stays REJECTED at TIER_0 due to Stage 4 trend damage and the breached $116.28 stop. Second, sell all 17.764 shares in Charles Schwab via market or tight limit order (~$1,839.82 proceeds), realizing the -$1,160.17 loss cleanly rather than risking a parity slide toward $81.58.

Third, park 100% of those settled proceeds in Schwab money-market or T-bill cash (~4.76% 2-year benchmark), keeping Shortlist leader McKesson and outside peer Micron at 0%. Keep SKHY on your calendar for January 27–28, 2027 Q4 earnings: if working capital collects cleanly, HBM4 margins hold, and shares carve a tight base across or above the $81.58–$93.48 monitor band before reclaiming $157.01 on >=35.5 million daily volume, we will re-underwrite the setup fresh.

Compare our portfolio posture before and after executing this plan. Before selling, $1,839.82 sits trapped in a high-volatility Stage 4 ADR (9.98% daily ATR, 8.11% weekly / 6.01% monthly Finviz volatility, beta '-') carrying a 27.0% Seoul parity premium and -35.7% Bear-regime fundamental stress expected value ($66.59). After executing EXIT_IMMEDIATELY, that capital earns ~4.76% risk-free yield in cash with zero drawdown risk while the S&P 500 works through its ten distribution days.

Every cyclical market eventually hands patient investors a clean Stage 1 base and a Stage 2 breakout on strong breadth. By enforcing our breached $116.28 stop today and refusing to average down into Stage 4, we preserve both our capital and our objectivity for when SK hynix's next confirmed uptrend begins.

Stay disciplined with every alert and dollar level above. Once the Schwab sell order fills and the $1,839.82 settles into cash, your portfolio is completely protected against any slide toward Pivot S2 ($93.48), Seoul KRX parity ($81.58), or the $60.06 1.87x KRX P/B stress floor, and dry powder stands ready for the next market uptrend.
